title: Love 2.0: How to Fix Your Marriage, Part 1

sentences.en: Hidden Brain turns 10 this year, and to celebrate, we're bringing the show to cities across the United States and Canada in a live performance.
sentences.zh: Hidden Brain 今年成立十周年了，为了庆祝，我们将把节目带到美国和加拿大的多个城市进行现场演出。

sentences.en: Our next stops are in Baltimore on October 11th, Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我们的下一站是 10 月 11 日的巴尔的摩，华盛顿特区

sentences.en: on October 12th, and Los Angeles on November 22nd.
sentences.zh: 是 10 月 12 日，洛杉矶是 11 月 22 日。

sentences.en: Join me as I share seven key psychological insights from the show's first decade.
sentences.zh: 欢迎加入我，我将分享节目开播十年来的七个关键心理学见解。

sentences.en: For more information and tickets, go to hiddenbrain.org slash tour.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息并购买门票，请访问 hiddenbrain.org 斜杠 tour。

sentences.en: I hope to see you there.
There comes a time in most relationships when people look at the partner sitting across the table from them and think,
sentences.zh: 大多数关系中都会有这样一个时刻：人们看着坐在桌子对面的伴侣，心想：

sentences.en: Maybe you don't like the way your partner eats with his mouth open.
sentences.zh: 也许你不喜欢伴侣张着嘴吃饭的样子。

sentences.en: Maybe you don't like the way she's always working.
sentences.zh: 也许你不喜欢她总是忙于工作。

sentences.en: Maybe you don't like, well, lots of things.
sentences.zh: 也许你不喜欢……嗯，很多事情。

sentences.en: At moments like this, a thought crosses our minds.
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，一个念头会闪过我们的脑海。

sentences.en: Perhaps we can get our partners to close their mouths while they eat.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以让伴侣吃饭时闭上嘴。

sentences.en: Perhaps we can get them to have more work-life balance.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以让他们实现更好的工作与生活平衡。

sentences.en: Perhaps we can change them into a better version of themselves.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以把他们变成更好的自己。

sentences.en: We know exactly what needs to be done, and we know exactly how to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们清楚地知道需要做什么，也清楚地知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: We'll first explain, very politely, of course, how our partners are doing things wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们首先会非常礼貌地解释伴侣哪里做得不对。

sentences.en: We'll show them how they can be better.
sentences.zh: 我们会向他们展示如何变得更好。

sentences.en: If they fail to listen, we'll go back and try again.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不听，我们会再试一次。

sentences.en: Maybe add a wagging finger, a slightly raised voice.
sentences.zh: 也许会加上摇晃的手指，稍微提高嗓门。

sentences.en: With patience, persistence, and a little punishment, we can get our partners to change their ways.
sentences.zh: 只要有耐心、毅力，再加一点惩罚，我们就能让伴侣改掉他们的习惯。
我们所有的烦恼都会消失。

sentences.en: The flutes of heaven will play sweet music,
sentences.zh: 天堂的笛声将奏出美妙的音乐，

sentences.en: and we will get to live in the romantic paradise we deserve.
sentences.zh: 我们将生活在我们应得的浪漫天堂里。

sentences.en: Maybe, instead of changing your partner, you end up in mutual recrimination.
sentences.zh: 也许，你最终得到的不是伴侣的改变，而是相互指责。

sentences.en: Instead of the flutes of heaven, you get fights.
sentences.zh: 你得到的不是天堂的笛声，而是争吵。

sentences.en: Instead of change, you get obstinacy.
sentences.zh: 你得到的不是改变，而是固执。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, and in a companion story on Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 本周的 Hidden Brain，以及 Hidden Brain Plus 的配套故事中，

sentences.en: we're going to bring you the first episode in a month-long series, all about love.
sentences.zh: 我们将为您带来为期一个月的系列节目的第一集，主题全是关于爱。

sentences.en: We'll explore the expectations we put on our relationships,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨我们对人际关系的期望，

sentences.en: and how our society's views on romance and marriage have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 以及我们社会对浪漫和婚姻的看法是如何随时间变化的。

sentences.en: We'll also look at the anatomy of a breakup,
sentences.zh: 我们还将剖析分手的本质，

sentences.en: and ways to soften the blow when love comes to an end.
sentences.zh: 以及当爱情走到尽头时减轻痛苦的方法。

sentences.en: That's all to come over the next few weeks as part of our Love 2.0 series.
sentences.zh: 这些内容将在接下来的几周内作为我们“爱 2.0”系列的一部分呈现。

sentences.en: Today, we kick things off with a deep dive into the art and science of mending troubled relationships.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们以深入探讨修复问题关系的艺术与科学作为开端。

sentences.en: We'll explore a radically different path from the one we usually choose,
sentences.zh: 我们将探索一条与我们通常选择的截然不同的道路，

sentences.en: a path that scientific research shows might actually work.
sentences.zh: 一条科学研究表明可能真正有效的道路。

sentences.en: Love songs and romantic poetry are full of images of two people becoming one in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 情歌和浪漫诗歌中充满了两人在一段关系中合二为一的意象。

sentences.en: But something that makes relationships difficult is that we remain, to some extent, stubbornly ourselves,
sentences.zh: 但让关系变得困难的一点是，我们在某种程度上仍然固执地保持着自我，

sentences.en: not one seamless entity, but two distinctive and sometimes prickly individuals.
sentences.zh: 不是一个无缝的整体，而是两个独特且有时带刺的个体。

sentences.en: All of us intuitively know how to fix this problem.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都凭直觉知道如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The title of a long-running musical that premiered in 1996 captures the experience of many couples.
sentences.zh: 一部 1996 年首演的长青音乐剧的标题捕捉到了许多伴侣的经历。

sentences.en: It was titled, I Love You, You're Perfect, Now Change.
sentences.zh: 剧名是《我爱你，你很完美，现在改改吧》。

sentences.en: At Clark University, psychologist James Cordova studies the dynamics of relationships.
sentences.zh: 在克拉克大学，心理学家 James Cordova 研究人际关系的动态。

sentences.en: For many years, he has studied a different approach to the one we usually use.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他研究了一种与我们通常使用的方法不同的方法。

sentences.en: James Cordova, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: James Cordova，欢迎来到 Hidden Brain。

sentences.en: It's so great to be here.
James, I understand that you're a person who loves to josh around and tease people in a humorous way.
sentences.zh: James，我听说你是一个喜欢开玩笑、以幽默方式逗弄别人的人。

sentences.en: What happens when you engage this side of your personality with your wife?
sentences.zh: 当你对妻子展现这一面时会发生什么？

sentences.en: So, yeah, I was raised in a community where one of the ways that we show love and affection for each other
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我是在一个社区长大的，我们表达爱和感情的方式之一

sentences.en: is just ongoing joshing and teasing of each other.
sentences.zh: 就是不断地互相开玩笑和逗弄。

sentences.en: So this is just part of who I am in relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是我在关系中性格的一部分。

sentences.en: And as it turns out, my wife is much too tenderhearted for that kind of ongoing teasing.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我妻子的心太软，受不了那种持续的逗弄。

sentences.en: I understand that you've sometimes made jokes and you have inadvertently hurt her feelings?
sentences.zh: 我听说你有时开玩笑，无意中伤害了她的感情？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, this was something that, because it comes so naturally to me,
sentences.zh: 是的，不，这是因为这对我来说太自然了，

sentences.en: it took years for me to really develop a sensitivity in that spot.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几年时间才真正培养出那方面的敏感度。

sentences.en: I understand this dynamic played out between the two of you once when you went shopping together
sentences.zh: 我听说有一次你们在新墨西哥州圣达菲一起购物时，这种动态就上演了。
James，请告诉我当时的情况以及发生了什么。

sentences.en: Give me both the context for what happened and what happened, James.

sentences.zh: 当时我们正在为她买一双新靴子。

sentences.en: So we were in the process of shopping for a new pair of boots for her.
sentences.zh: 我们之间有一个类似内部笑话的东西，

sentences.en: And one of the things that we have is sort of like an inside joke between the two of us
sentences.zh: 那就是她的品味非常高。

sentences.en: is that she has an exquisite taste.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们购物时，她十有八九会直奔最昂贵的版本。

sentences.en: So way more often than not, when we're shopping for something, she makes a beeline for the most expensive version
sentences.zh: 这是我们之间一个持续不断的笑话。

sentences.en: of whatever it is that we're shopping for.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时买靴子买得很开心，

sentences.en: And it's an ongoing sort of running joke between the two of us.
sentences.zh: 正走进圣达菲一家精品靴子店。

sentences.en: So we were having a good time shopping for boots,
sentences.zh: 当我们走进去时，我冲店主喊道：

sentences.en: and we're heading into this like small kind of boutique boot store in Santa Fe.
sentences.zh: “你能直接给我们看看店里最贵的一双靴子，省点时间吗？”

sentences.en: And so as we're walking in, I call out to the proprietor and I say,
sentences.zh: 我以为我妻子会觉得这很有趣，但显然在那一刻她并没有。

sentences.en: can you just go ahead and show us the most expensive pair of boots in the store and save us some time?
Which I thought my wife would find hilarious, but clearly in the moment did not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我的妻子受伤时，她会变得安静，对吧？
所以语气发生了非常明显的转变，从我们进门时那种俏皮和轻松，

sentences.en: So, you know, when my wife is hurt, she gets quiet, right?
sentences.zh: 到你可以感觉到她在退缩。

sentences.en: So there's a very distinct shift in tone from the sort of playfulness and lightheartedness
sentences.zh: 我假设那时你意识到自己说错话了。

sentences.en: that we were experiencing as we were walking in the door
to you can just sort of feel her pull away.
I'm assuming at that point you realized that you had put your foot in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到，发生了什么事。
有趣的是，我的本能还是想看看能不能保持那种势头，对吧？
所以，哦，我们玩得很开心，我们互相开着玩笑，

sentences.en: I can tell, like, something happened.
sentences.zh: 发生了点什么，但也许我可以继续这种俏皮，

sentences.en: And it's interesting because, like, my instinct is still to see if I can maintain the momentum, right?
So, oh, we were having a good time, we were feeling jokey with each other,
sentences.zh: 结果证明，这通常行不通。

sentences.en: and something happened, but maybe I can just, like, keep going with the playfulness
sentences.zh: 所以多年来，你实际上一直在劝说你的妻子在面对你的逗弄时放轻松点。
你对她说了什么，她有什么反应？

sentences.en: And, you know, that just, as it turns out, doesn't usually work.
sentences.zh: 我试着解释我的出发点。

sentences.en: So over the years, you have actually nudged your wife to lighten up when it comes to your teasing.
sentences.zh: 比如，这只是表达爱意的一种方式，而且很俏皮。

sentences.en: What have you said to her and how has she reacted?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，她显然认识我的朋友和家人，

sentences.en: So, like, I've tried to, like, explain where I'm coming from.
sentences.zh: 也见过这种互动在其他人身上发生。

sentences.en: Like, this is just by way of being affectionate and it's playful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她明白，但这招对她不管用，对吧？

sentences.en: And, like, you know, she obviously knows my friends and my family
sentences.zh: 所以我试着帮她从我的角度去理解，

sentences.en: and has seen that play out between other folks.
sentences.zh: 结果却像铅球一样沉重，完全没用。

sentences.en: And, I mean, she gets it, but it just doesn't work for her, right?
sentences.zh: James，除了作为研究员，你还是一位在心理治疗中与伴侣合作的临床医生。

sentences.en: So I've tried to, like, help her understand it from my perspective,
sentences.zh: 有一对伴侣中，妻子非常希望丈夫敞开心扉谈论他的感受，

sentences.en: which has just gone over like a lead balloon.
So in addition to being a researcher, James, you're also a clinician who works with couples in psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 这种冲突在他们之间是如何上演的？

sentences.en: One couple featured a woman who really wanted her husband to open up and talk about his feelings,
sentences.zh: 在这对伴侣中，妻子非常深刻地感觉到丈夫在对她隐瞒，对吧？
她想知道他的感受，让他谈谈他的愿望和需求，

sentences.en: How did this conflict play out between them?
sentences.zh: 以及他的起起落落，而他非常隐忍，几乎只说单音节词，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, in this particular couple, the wife felt, like, quite deeply that her husband was withholding from her, right?
sentences.zh: 显然他爱她，但他的爱的语言是服务行为，而不是谈论感受。

sentences.en: That she wanted to be able to know what he was feeling, have him talk to her about his wants and needs
sentences.zh: 她会尝试，他会感到被评判，然后他们就会背对彼此。

sentences.en: and his ups and downs, and he was just very much a stoic, you know, very, you know, almost monosyllabic, right?
sentences.zh: 她试了几次，然后沮丧地放弃了，他感到被评判，就走开了。

sentences.en: You know, clearly loved her, but his love language was acts of service, not necessarily talking about his feelings.
sentences.zh: 你称之为“豪猪-乌龟困境”。

sentences.en: And, you know, she would try, and he would feel judged, and then they would, you know, sort of turn away from each other.
sentences.zh: 你说的这个短语是什么意思？

sentences.en: You know, she'd try a few times and then give up in frustration, and he would feel judged and just sort of wander off.
sentences.zh: 我们在伴侣身上经常看到的一种模式是，当他们之间发生冲突时，他们如何反应。

sentences.en: You call this a porcupine-turtle conundrum.
sentences.zh: 出现了一些让人感到紧张、受伤或痛苦的事情。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that phrase?
sentences.zh: 当事情痛苦时，我们人类最自然的反应通常是战斗或逃跑的某种版本。

sentences.en: So, one of the patterns that we often see in couples is how they respond when there is conflict between the two of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有些人更倾向于战斗。

sentences.en: So something comes up that feels tense or hurtful or painful in some way.
And our natural human reaction when something is painful most often is some version of either fight or flight.
sentences.zh: 当发生冲突时，我们会竖起刺，冲向伴侣。

sentences.en: And so some of us lean a little bit more in the direction of fight.
sentences.zh: 内心的感觉是：我要通过面对问题并与之抗争来解决它。
而对于我们中的其他人，我们更像乌龟。

sentences.en: When we're having conflict, we pull our quills out, we push our quills out, and we go toward our partner.
sentences.zh: 我们学会了对痛苦采取更倾向于逃跑的反应。

sentences.en: The sense inside of that is I'm going to resolve this problem by moving towards it and fighting it.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们感到冲突或评判的压力时，我们会安静下来。

sentences.en: And for others of us, we're more like turtles.
We've learned something more of a flight response to feeling pain.
So when we're feeling that stress of conflict or judgment, we get quiet.
sentences.zh: 有时实际上是离开房间。
这种模式会出现，它可以朝任何方向发展。
如果乌龟感觉到豪猪的刺出来了，它们就开始退缩。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's actually literally leaving the room.
sentences.zh: 这种退缩让豪猪感到威胁。

sentences.en: And the pattern emerges such that it can happen in either direction.
sentences.zh: 所以那个人会更用力地追赶，刺竖得更厉害，攻击性更强，这让另一个人更深地缩进壳里。

sentences.en: If the turtle feels the porcupine's quills coming out, they start to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 这对他们俩来说都很令人沮丧，对吧？

sentences.en: That withdrawal feels threatening to the porcupine.
sentences.zh: 壳里的人在等豪猪停止戳我，

sentences.en: So that person pursues even harder with their quills out even more aggressively, which makes the other person pull into their shell even more deeply.
sentences.zh: 而扮演豪猪角色的人则拼命想让对方从壳里出来。

sentences.en: And it's frustrating for both of them, right?
sentences.zh: 我们可以一直进行那种豪猪-乌龟模式，直到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: The person in the shell is waiting for the porcupine to stop poking me,
sentences.zh: 对大多数伴侣来说，这就是模式的终结方式。

sentences.en: and the person who's in the porcupine role is just desperate for the other person to come back out of their shell.
sentences.zh: 我们只是做下去，直到累得再也做不动了。

sentences.en: And we can engage that kind of porcupine-turtle pattern until we're exhausted.
sentences.zh: James，你合作的另一对伴侣遇到了不同的问题。

sentences.en: And that's, for most couples, how the pattern resolves.
sentences.zh: 在这里，丈夫一心想让妻子保持身材和健康。

sentences.en: We just do it until we're too tired to do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 那种动态是如何上演的？

sentences.en: There was another couple you worked with who struggled with a different problem, James.
sentences.zh: 这是一对我不时会见到的伴侣。

sentences.en: Here, the husband was preoccupied with his wife being fit and in shape.
How did that dynamic play out?
sentences.zh: 几乎总是由她发起，因为她对他的要求感到非常受伤，

sentences.en: This is a couple that I've seen somewhat regularly.
sentences.zh: 他鼓励她多运动、变得更健康、注意饮食的方式并不高明，对吧？

sentences.en: They come in, I would say, once a year or so.
sentences.zh: 他脑子里有一种特定体型的形象，他说，我没办法，

sentences.en: And almost always initiated, coming into therapy will be initiated by her because she is feeling so hurt by his requests for, his demands for,
sentences.zh: 我就是被这种体型吸引。

sentences.en: his not particularly skillful encouragement for her to exercise more, become more fit, watch what she eats, right?
sentences.zh: 而他的妻子其实很健康。

sentences.en: And he has this image in mind of a particular kind of physique that he says, I mean, I can't help it.
sentences.zh: 她只是普通女性的健康，不是超级名模那种健康。

sentences.en: This is just what I'm attracted to.
sentences.zh: 他们会陷入这种僵局，她试图安抚，试图顺从，试图抵制。

sentences.en: And his wife is actually quite fit.
sentences.zh: 而他只是在投射这种挫败感和失望感，老实说，还带有一点羞耻感。

sentences.en: She's just normal woman fit, not like supermodel fit.
sentences.zh: 当这种模式变得棘手时，他们无法从中走出来。

sentences.en: And they will get stuck in this place where, you know, she tries to appease, she tries to go along, she tries to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们无法摆脱这种模式。

sentences.en: And he just is projecting this experience of frustration and disappointment, honestly tinged with a little bit of shame.
sentences.zh: 他们无法摆脱这种模式。

sentences.en: And they can't get themselves out of this pattern when it gets sticky for them.
sentences.zh: 他们无法摆脱这种模式。

sentences.en: I'm imagining that each person has tried to change the behavior of the other.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都曾尝试改变对方的行为。

sentences.en: You clearly indicated how the husband is trying to change the behavior of the wife.
sentences.zh: 你清楚地指出了丈夫是如何试图改变妻子的行为的。

sentences.en: But has the reverse happened as well?
sentences.zh: 但反过来是否也发生过呢？

sentences.en: So her, you know, her strong attempts are to help him see that this is what a normal person's fit body looks like, to get him to let go of that desire, or at least to, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，她强烈的尝试是为了让他明白，这才是正常人健康体魄的样子，让他放下那种渴望，或者至少，我想，

sentences.en: if he can't let go of it, to keep it to himself.
sentences.zh: 如果他无法放下，至少也要藏在心里。

sentences.en: When we face a problem in our relationships, the solution often seems simple.
sentences.zh: 当我们面对关系中的问题时，解决方案往往看起来很简单。

sentences.en: Obviously, our partners need to change.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们的伴侣需要改变。

sentences.en: When we come back, when our efforts to change another person work, and when they don't, and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨我们改变他人的努力何时有效，何时无效，以及我们能做些什么。

sentences.en: Most long-term relationships eventually uncover sharp angles and jagged edges.
sentences.zh: 大多数长期关系最终都会暴露出尖锐的棱角和粗糙的边缘。

sentences.en: Things that one person does or doesn't do drive the other person bonkers.
sentences.zh: 一个人做或不做某些事，会让另一个人抓狂。

sentences.en: At Clark University, psychologist James Cordover has studied the science of behavior change, when it works, when it doesn't, and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 在克拉克大学，心理学家 James Cordover 研究了行为改变的科学：它何时有效，何时无效，以及我们能做些什么。

sentences.en: James, you say that for a long time, the emphasis within the field of couples therapy was on helping couples change their behavior.
sentences.zh: James，你说长期以来，夫妻治疗领域的重点一直在于帮助夫妻改变他们的行为。

sentences.en: Now, this must have fit with the assumption that most couples themselves have,
sentences.zh: 这一定符合大多数夫妻自己所持有的假设，

sentences.en: which is that the problems in their relationships would disappear if only the other person would change.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果对方能改变，他们关系中的问题就会消失。

sentences.en: That is our natural instinct, right?

sentences.zh: 而你就是那个问题所在。

sentences.en: And if you would change, I would feel better.
sentences.zh: 如果你能改变，我就会感觉好些。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, of course, that's the way couples come in.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，当然，这就是夫妻们来咨询时的状态。

sentences.en: And, you know, warm-hearted, beneficent therapists tried to meet them right there in the thing that they were asking for.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，热心肠、善良的治疗师们试图在他们所要求的层面上满足他们。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, there must be times when, in fact, this approach does work.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，事实上肯定有这种方法奏效的时候吧。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, couples are coming in, and presumably they're trying to recruit.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，夫妻们来咨询时，大概是想拉拢治疗师。

sentences.en: Each of them is trying to recruit the therapist onto their side to tell the other person what they're doing wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都试图拉拢治疗师站在自己这边，去告诉对方他们做错了什么。

sentences.en: But there must be times where therapists, in fact, are successful at getting couples to change their behavior?
sentences.zh: 但肯定有治疗师成功让夫妻改变行为的时候吧？

sentences.en: I was originally trained in what was called behavioral marital therapy, which was very much a change-oriented approach to doing couple therapy.
sentences.zh: 我最初接受的是所谓的行为婚姻治疗培训，这是一种非常注重改变的夫妻治疗方法。

sentences.en: And the changes that we would work on with couples is increasing the frequency with which they were doing nice things for each other.
sentences.zh: 我们与夫妻共同努力的改变，是增加他们为彼此做贴心事的频率。

sentences.en: We call it that behavior exchange.
Teaching them how to communicate more effectively.
sentences.zh: 教他们如何更有效地沟通。

sentences.en: Teaching them how to problem-solve more effectively.
sentences.zh: 教他们如何更有效地解决问题。

sentences.en: But as it turned out, even though it is a therapy that has demonstrable effectiveness, none of those skills would follow couples home.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，尽管这是一种具有显著疗效的治疗方法，但这些技能并不能跟随夫妻回到家中。

sentences.en: So there is some change happening, but it's difficult for couples to sustain it.
sentences.zh: 所以确实发生了一些改变，但夫妻们很难维持下去。

sentences.en: Couples, of course, do solve problems all the time.
sentences.zh: 当然，夫妻们确实一直在解决问题。

sentences.en: That's because many problems have an easy solution.
sentences.zh: 那是因为许多问题都有简单的解决方案。

sentences.en: When we first get together, we're adjusting to each other.
sentences.zh: 当我们刚在一起时，我们正在互相适应。

sentences.en: And the things that are easy to adjust to, we adjust to so quickly that we almost don't even notice that we've done it.
sentences.zh: 那些容易适应的事情，我们适应得如此之快，以至于几乎没有意识到我们已经做到了。

sentences.en: Like, which side of the bed are you going to sleep on?

sentences.en: Which side of the bed am I going to sleep on?
And then just above that are what I think of as like mezzanine-level problems that we might have to struggle with a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后，在此之上的是我所认为的“夹层级”问题，我们可能需要为此挣扎一下。

sentences.en: Sometimes they take weeks, months, or years.

sentences.en: But we do eventually solve them, and then we're good.

sentences.en: the ones that are not simple to solve, but also are not intractable.
sentences.zh: 那些解决起来不简单，但也并非棘手到无法解决的问题。

sentences.en: He told me of a time he and his wife had a dispute over his love for cycling.

sentences.en: One is I've become something of an endorphin addict, so it's just like it's a necessary part of who I am.

sentences.en: And two, bike riding like road cycling is dangerous.
